text: You duck past notices encouraging temperance and restraint as you enter the bar. Someone is playing a stringed instrument in an alcove. A row of handworked samovars suggests that tea is served as often as the weak grain-brew favored by the local spacer crews at the bar. Many of the patrons at tables or booths seem to be long-haulers or the few stationed nonbelievers huddling in the closest analog to a den of sin that can be found.
You stay clear of the Knights of Ludd and they do not hinder your passage. Though you are ever watched by their patrols, comms are crisp and polite.
Requests for your destination and purpose are notably lessened, if not absent. You respect their sometimes archaic protocols and they occasionally fail to scowl at your lifestyle.

The Knights of Ludd watch you with less suspicion than most spacers, and the Church welcomes you to the volumes they control. You are an old hand at navigating their ways of operating and leave behind those technologies which cause alarm to the most wary Knights.

You are given preferential treatment over other spacers during security checks and are allowed to self-moderate unsubtle use of technologies without need for the heavy hand of the Knights of Ludd to guide you toward righteousness.

The Knights of Ludd put great trust in your handling of technology for righteous cause. Your presence is seen as a boon to security and your sensor data packages are integrated into sector models. Even the most radical of Knights acknowledge your contribution.

You are seen as a typical spacer; dismissive of Ludd's revelation and scornful of the Church. The Knights of Ludd remind you of the moral importance of Technological Correctness during every tense interaction.

The Knights look warily upon you, and subject you to unnecessary delays and investigation. Curates of the Church of Galactic Redemption offer you as example of one led far astray from Ludd's revelation; one lost in the machine; perhaps not yet lost to Moloch, but an unwitting servant to evil.

The Church considers you a minion of Moloch, a slave to demonic technology. You are a witless ally of Mammon, and the Knights treat you as an agent of evil. Begone, or be subject to the wrath of the righteous.

You have been deemed an unholy foe. An Inquisitor has been assigned to carry out your termination, which they will name a righteous deed, just and honorable. The Knights' indoctrinal school for squires identifies you as the slavering dretch of every known demon, from Mammon, Moloch, and Belial all the way down to some possibly created just for you.

After an indeterminate time waiting for a response, the comm-link connects you with what appears to be one of the Grandmaster's squires. Though clearly not a knight, they nonetheless manage to carry enough authority to keep you paying attention.
"Greetings," the squire says. "The Grandmaster is currently not receiving any visitors at this time. If this is an urgent matter, please speak with one of the Knights."

text: Your attempt to secure an audience with the Grandmaster falls on deaf ears as the squire bluntly turns you down.
"The Grandmaster wishes not to be disturbed. Only those who have an standing invitation to meet with the Grandmaster may do so at this time."

After some time waiting, you reach the office of the Chaptermaster. There's a perfunctory greeting before you're pushed off the line with instructions to contact an underling if looking for freelance writs. No doubt dealings with her will require building some trust within the organization first. Perhaps the Knight-Leader has some work.

Sister Rebecca Greenflight answers the comm herself, which you suspect is rare. The office behind her is spare: a reliquary on a shelf, a wall of sealed files, a narrow window full of the Eos gate.

"Captain. The Office of Agents keeps no public hours, and I keep fewer." She studies you without hurry. "If you have something the Order should know, say it plainly. If not, I will not keep you."

"Blessings on you, $PlayerSirOrMadam. I regret that we're quite inundated over here. If you're looking for work, please contact one of the administrators, they have reliable contracts for our commissioned freelancers; the faith has many that we must defend against who would see it brought low. 

Our Master of Agents on our sister-station Lyra may also need a lead investigated. 

Visit me again sometime soon and we may have some formal contracts ready."

"Till next we meet, Captain!"

Ah, another thing, Captain. Perhaps if you're the valiant type, you can find our expeditions gather about twice a month, as soon as one returns, or... if we lose contact. Please, if you provide them escort they're sure to go somewhere interesting. You'd be doing us a great favor. Blessings upon you, Captain.
There is no response, only the sense of some burning menace sizing up its targets.

As your $shipOrFleet moves into a close holding orbit, your comms officer murmurs, "Hardly any bleed at all coming from that station, Captain. If it didn't have mass, we'd never..." They trail off, squinting at their console.

The bridge sounds an alert as a single ship detaches from the station hull and accelerates towards your fleet. A comms notification chimes, moments later. Without waiting, your officer scans and plays the message; a man's voice, reedy and distracted, talks over the alarms.

"You have violated an information blackout area. Don't try to run. It'll interfere with the data collection."

You seize the initiative and order an approach vector before the station's defenders have a chance to throw any more surprises your way.

It's when you've closed half the distance to the station that your sensor officer yells out in alarm - a spike in subspace tearing through the display. A moment later the station lights up on your monitor like the Rings of Maxios as whatever technology that was cloaking its signal dispels from your feeds. Your salvor crew chirps in excitement - not only is the station clearly loaded with technology, it's all active. Your crew chief and science officer cry out in exultation of the record haul.

You watch as the station glows and glitters before you with untapped promise - and then one by one each glowing node on the sensor disappears, alarms appearing as energy surges flare throughout the station, culminating in a single massive eruption along the station's main axis that shatters it utterly.

Your officers mournfully gawk as their treasure vanishes like swarmers meandering into a flak field. The secrecy of whatever was being researched here was clearly worth the entire station's sacrifice, and an educated guess tells you the strange ship you fought had a lot to do with it. 

You restrain your salvors until you're sure your $shipOrFleet has a clean approach path into the wreckage, then set to the furious recovery work.

The post-mortem reveals that the spike in the subspace readings was due to a small phase shuttle leaping out of the system, and the drop in sensor cloaking was due to the internal systems surging and breaking. Frustratingly, the occupants were professional - everything that might contain any information on them was wiped clean from the lowest memory key to the vitally important delta-AI managing the station life support systems. However, what's clear is that this was a Tri-Tachyon operation, and Tri-Tachyon executives always have some dirt on the others, hiding them off the main systems and hidden away in shielded compartments.

It doesn't take your crew long to locate a mag-safe box underneath the paneling in an engineering section, containing a memory key wrapped in organic-derived insulation. The Cache is obstinantly bio-locked, and only select sections of the key can be scraped off. Apart from some scandalous corporate gossip and contextless financial records, you locate only a few intact records, about one "Project Dusk."

text:
The frigate before you appears to be some variant of the Tri-Tachyon Hyperion, though its design is otherwise exotic. Well, even more exotic. A comm request comes through from the strange vessel and your comms officer brings it to your display. 

"Interloper. You have come for what is not yours. Power down and you will not be unnecessarily harmed."

The link cuts. A warning or a threat, and from a fully coherent AI core. Great. Perhaps the ship that didn't speak was preferrable. Shaking off these thoughts, you issue the orders to your bridge crew.

The frigate before you appears to be some variant of the Tri-Tachyon Hyperion, though its design is otherwise exotic. Well, even more exotic.

There appear to be small, bright EM sources, "-Only partially overlapping the visual spectrum," your sensors officer reports. They orbit with uncanny motion around the strange vessel. Your bridge crew murmurs speculation between their stations: some kind of point defense field? Microsat thruster bursts? The speculation is far from concensus. A ping from the comm panel rings out before you can ponder further.

"Interloper. You have come for what is not yours. Power down and you will not be unnecessarily harmed."

The link cuts as abruptly as it began. A threat from a fully coherent AI core. Great. A moment goes by but your attention lingers on some far away sound - as if catching a melody on the wind. When you attempt to focus on the harmony the impression evaporates as quickly as it came. Gathering yourself, you issue the orders to your bridge crew.

The vicious frigate finally ignites in a superheated conflagration, much to your relief. There are no further signals from the local volume, you hear only the hasty chatter of damage assessments and status reports from your bridge crew. Whatever the hell that was, it's over.
The broken frigate, now quite lifeless, is drifting through space.

Salvage teams hook their tethers into the fragmented vessel's hull and get to work. Tense minutes pass until the chatter from the boarding party picks up in excitement.

"$PlayerSirOrMadam, this ship is astounding - the level of sophistication, and the design! It's like stepping into an alien world!" The chief takes a moment to recover some of his professionalism before continuing.

"The command pod was destroyed, or scuttled, and there's no sign of other crew, but other systems are mostly intact. We don't understand how a piece of this thing works but the interfaces seem normal enough." 

He continues quickly. "Together we've recovered an entry in the systems from the ship's last refit - it was recent. The location's out in the fringes, nothing on record, but this would indicate there's some kind of facility out there. There could be more of this tech! Here, I'm sending what we've got."

It seems someone's excited by the find, and you can't deny its magnitude, but there's no doubt in your mind that wherever this instrument came from will be yet more fiercely guarded than this cache. Is it really worth provoking the worst of the corporation to delve its darkest secrets? It's not too late to forget this ship and move on...

Your crew lead resumes before you can get overwhelmed in your thoughts.

"From what we can determine - which, granted, isn't that much - the ship's systems are mostly compatible with our own. We'll need a lot of our supplies, and time, but we could try to restore operation," he reports in both eagerness and trepidation, "just give us the word."

The Flagship of the Tri-Tachyon fleet superficially resembles the hull of a Doom cruiser, but what heritage this monstrosity shares with that hull is most certainly long diverged. Dooms are bad enough, this thing can only mean trouble.

The small, bright motes orbiting the vessel are but an afterthought before the Tri-Tachyon defense fleet. Your tactical thought processes are interrupted by your comm panel lighting up.

"Power down and you will not be unnecessarily harmed," the voice intones before the signal cuts.

Short, to the point, and backed up by an armada's firepower - if you weren't on the receiving end you might like their style. Wasting no time, you begin issuing tactical orders to your bridge crew.

The burning wreckage of the Tri-Tachyon black fleet litters the local volume, each of the defenders painstakingly reduced to inert jumbles of alloys and slag. Whatever treasure awaits you here, there is only it, your fleet, and fresh wreckage for light years in any direction.

Your eye catches on a datacore glinting in the debris that must have broken free during the fight. Perhaps they didn't have time to fully scrub it. You give a nod to your salvors and in short order it's brought on board.
Prepare yourself, this foe will be unlike any you have faced before.

On approach one of your officers notes a distant glow, a surge of energy originating from the opposing fleet. The bridge crew immediately springs to action, manning consoles and barking orders, only to falter as the view from the bridge slowly turns into a cascade of blinding white. Hull-mounted sensor equipment declares incandescence across the entire electromagnetic spectrum before the readings distort into incomprehension. Amidst a song of light and fire, Amaterasu beckons.

The looming Elysian fleet closes in. At its head is a carrier unlike any you have yet seen, leading a flock of white wings. Without warning a red haze spills over the Elysian vessels as if springing forth from the Abyssal singularity itself. 
On a canvas of crimson a myriad of silhouettes fly forth like gleaming stars in a murdered sky. The commlink crackles with a noise that can't be distinguished from static or from singing. The Heart welcomes you into its scarlet grip.

The moment the drivefields interlock, a change in movement is reported from the opposing fleet. Feedback from the comms becomes a deafening din as a torrent of positional instructions pours across every channel. Ship after ship slams into formation. The din fuses into a drone, a clarion call that shakes your bones until the communications officer manages to get the order for total system shutdown across. Sensors observe the million pinpricks of slaved salvor units lifting off, taking up position behind the fleet. Like a flock of vultures waiting to pick your bones clean. Like an army on the march, Nian hungers.

text: The angular, utilitarian structure of Nomios Rapid Autofab stands ahead, its industrial modules buzzing with the constant activity of projects that need to be turned around quickly. This station thrives on efficiency, handling smaller, high-priority tasks for the sector’s major factions - aside from one notable exception. Here, prototypes and specialized components are built at speed, driven by the need to meet tight deadlines. A few engineering vessels and freighters shuttle between bays, ensuring that every project keeps moving toward completion, no matter how tight the schedule.

As your ship nears, you transmit a docking request, but the response is quick and professional. "Captain, this facility is restricted to authorized personnel and faction contracts. Without a direct referral or specific business with Mbaye-Gogol, we cannot grant docking clearance." The voice remains polite, but firm. "For general work or services, I'd recommend heading down to the planet Nomios itself. Safe travels." The channel cuts off, and your ship’s course shifts away, the station receding into the backdrop of Arcadia.

The docking procedure is swift, almost routine now. "Welcome back, Captain $playerName," the voice over the comms greets you, professional but with a hint of recognition. Your ship is guided smoothly into a private berth. While the station continues its business as usual, there’s a subtle sense that the relic recovery represents something special - an opportunity that might grow in importance, depending on what the station’s engineers can eventually unlock from these ancient ships. A polite message from the liaison invites you to use the station's facilities before heading out again.

As you send your docking request, a quick response follows. "Captain $playerName, welcome. We’ve received word from Callisto Ibrahim about your arrival. Director Amadou Sembene is expecting you." The mention of the director himself catches you slightly off guard - this isn’t the kind of place where top leadership meets with just anyone. The docking queue opens, and your ship is smoothly guided to a private berth. Once docked, the subtle hum of the station's machinery fades, replaced by a message from a station liaison, inviting you to meet Sembene personally. It’s clear you’ve caught their interest - rarely does someone meet with the head of such a facility directly.

The Knight notices you reading and straightens, one thumb still pressing a tack home. "You are looking for work, captain? We are few, and the duties we keep are many. The Order asks for your service, not your faith." $HeOrShe waits for your answer with the patience of someone who has waited through a great many sermons.

The Knight nods, unoffended, and returns to $hisOrHer tacks. "Seek virtue, captain. The notice will keep."

A Knight-Captain answers your hail, his face cast in the staccato flicker of several open data slates. He does not look at the viewer immediately; his gaze is fixed on a scrolling manifest, his expression distant and severe. Around one wrist, a devotional cord is knotted tight.

"Brother Enarms. His light upon you," he says, still reading. Then the manifest scrolls out of frame and he sits straighter, like he only now remembers the camera. "$PlayerSirOrMadam. Forgive the delay. What can I do for you?"
"Captain $playerName." Enarms finishes the entry he is reading before he looks up. "What can I do for you?"
"Captain $playerName." The slate is already set aside, and he is looking straight at the screen. "Tell me this is good news. I am owed some."

"Captain $playerName." Enarms touches the cord at his wrist before he speaks, and does not seem to notice he has done it. He says something to someone off-frame, and a door closes somewhere behind him. "Providence has brought you back intact. Go on."
"Captain $playerName." Enarms looks up from his slate. "The raiders are still lying in wait, then. Two more traders turned back at Canaan this week." He does not make it an accusation.

"Captain $playerName." Enarms sets the slate down the moment the link opens. "You found them. I can see it." 

He waits, hands folded on the desk.
"Captain $playerName." A slate bearing Libra's seal sits on top of the stack at his elbow. Enarms turns it face-down before he speaks. "Their last courier was late again. What do you need?"
"Captain $playerName." Enarms' attention is already fixed on the screen. "You reached Libra." Not quite a question. "Tell me. Leave nothing out for my sake."

text: "Patience is a virtue the Order prizes, captain. One I suggest you cultivate. However... timeliness in the field is equally valuable. We will trust you can deliver."

"Indeed, we have work to offer." Enarms locks his gaze on a slate of shipping manifests and distress pings.

"Raiders, calling themselves the $kolPreludePirate_fleetName. Three of our traders and a pilgrim ship vanished since the turn of the cycle. Our last confirmed sighting: the $kolPreludePirate_systemName."

He looks up then. The lens is too honest about the shadows under his eyes.

"I'd send a patrol. I have one assembling now. It is currently: me." A pause, in case that was funny.

"Drive them off or break them, whichever the raiders allow. We will give you due reward; you will not be asked to take our vows of poverty."

Your boarding teams pull the raiders' data cores before the scuttling charges can finish their work. Most of it is the usual: fence contacts, stolen transponder codes, a pilgrim-ship manifest with the prices of the passengers marked.

text: "The Faith is eternal, captain, but the men who serve it are flawed. Today, we are reminded of that truth once more."

Enarms does not argue. "Perhaps." He looks at the slate for a while. 

"'Perhaps' is as far as I will go today, and further than I would like."
He nods slowly. "I had thought it. I had hoped no one would say it aloud." His hand comes into frame and lies flat on the slate, as if it might get up and harm him.
"Nothing. Forget you saw it." He hears himself. "No. I do not mean that. Do not forget it, but do not speak of it."

Martins has half turned to watch it. "Tell Enarms we're grateful. Tell him also that we see things out here Cygnus doesn't. Ships that aren't ours and aren't pirates, sitting at the edge of our guns and just... watching. They're getting bolder."

It is warm. There are plants: tomato vines on a trellis by the lamp, herbs in a long trough, a lemon tree in a ceramic pot that must have cost someone a great deal to bring up the well. A kettle ticks on a hotplate. Two good chairs face each other across a low table, and only one of them looks as though it has ever been sat in.

Enarms is by the trough with a watering can, in a clothspun shirt quite unlike the typical spacer's jumpsuit and, you note, better-made than most Luddic garb. He sets the can down when he sees you. "Captain. Welcome. Sit, please." He pours the tea without asking whether you want it.

Expeditions go out to the dark places to learn what waits there, and few come home with answers. Many don't come home at all. Patrols run double watches. The room has had visitors. The second chair has been sat in, and recently. Three cups are drying by the sink instead of one. The lemon tree has been moved off the table to the floor, to make room for something, and a data slate lies face-down on the table, its notification light still blinking.

Enarms is in armor this time, though his gloves are on the shelf beside the herbs. He does not offer an explanation, and the tea is already poured. "Tell me," he says.

You tell him: the star that is not a star, light bending the wrong way around it, and the ships. Not pirates; not anyone's patrol. Hulls sleeker than anything ever made by human hands, moving with a persistence no flesh and blood captain has.

Enarms listens without interrupting, his tea growing colder where it sits.

When you describe the fall, the dark star taking hold of your fleet and the strange sky on the far side of it, Enarms puts down his cup. For a while he says nothing at all.

"Creation is larger than our charts," he says at last, quietly. "We forget that. It is good to be reminded, and terrible." He does not ask you to describe it again.

"I recall ordering you to 'observe.'" It is not quite a rebuke. He looks you over as though expecting to find the damage on your hull. "You are here, so I will give thanks rather than a lecture. This time."

He rises and turns the face-down slate over, then thinks better of it and turns it back. "Mysterious ships scouting Libra. Mysterious ships keeping the anomaly. Machine-built and machine designed. Devices of Moloch." He says the name with intentional precision.

"There is a force, captain, reaching toward us out of the dark. And already the enemy within, compromising our strength. If they are one and the same..." He sits again, heavily. It goes unsaid. "This is beyond the two of us. Beyond a Knight-Captain's mandate. It has to go higher."

text:
The shuttle does not take you to Enarms' quarters. It sets down near the station's spine, and a pair of Knights in full combat plate walk you up a long ramp into a chamber that was once built as a chapel.

A dozen people sit in a half-ring of carved seats under the lamps: Knight-Leaders in their day-suits, an old curate with a censer smoking at her feet, two administrators with slates on their knees. At the center, in the highest chair, sits Master Helensis, gray-haired and very still.

Enarms stands at a lectern at the focus. He does not look at you as you are shown to a bench, but he brushes at the cord on his wrist. 

The curate leads a short prayer. Everyone bows their heads; you notice Helensis keeps her eyes open.

Enarms gives his report without ornament, and in order.
 A pirate band carrying the Order's true schedules, with a selection that could only come from intimate knowledge.
 Strange ships keeping watch on Libra.
 An anomaly in the dark where expeditions go and do not return, and machine-built hulls guarding it, beyond anything humanity has forged.

"I believe these reports are linked," he finishes. "Molochian creations, hostile to the Faith, and closing on us from several directions. I believe they are sizing us up. I do not believe they are in any hurry."

Murmurs travel around the half-ring and die out under Helensis' gaze.

"The Church has endured raiders since the first days of the Collapse, Brother," Helensis says. Her voice is mild and carries without effort.

"A few stolen schedules do not make a crusade. The Order is not so fragile that every shadow on a sensor screen is the Adversary come at last."

She lets that settle, then tilts her head. "And yet. I will not pretend these are a raider's mischief. Whatever watches us is not idle. The faithful are called to endure, yes. We are not called only to endure."

A Knight-Commander begins to answer; another cuts across him; the curate says something about prudence that nobody acknowledges. Helensis raises one finger and the room is quiet again. She turns to you. "You have seen these things with your own eyes, captain. What would you counsel?"

Helensis calls the question. The quorum declines, by a margin that is polite rather than close.

text:
For the first time the room goes properly still. Enarms stands still at his lectern.

"Libra," Helensis says. "Yes. Knightmaster Martins is a faithful servant, and has been faithful in that place for a very long time."

She holds for a deep breath. "That station is old, captain. Its equipment is older. To make it a fortress again would cost what this Order spends in a cycle, for a post on a fringe that guards nothing."

"We pray for Libra every week." She inclines her head toward the curate, who nods. "We cannot afford to do more. It is a sorrow, and we bear it." She does not sound as though she bears it heavily.

When the murmuring has run its course, Helensis gives the council's word. The matter is grave, and will be watched. It belongs, in the first instance, to the Knights' Inquisitors.

"You will take what you have seen to the Master of Agents at Star Keep Lyra," she tells you. "Sister Greenflight will know what to make of it, if anyone does."

The quorum assents without debate; it is the kind of decision that costs nothing.

Then, as the Knights begin to rise, she adds: "And since you are so willing, captain, there is one more thing. These machines you've found. They are an enemy we do not understand. Bring us pieces of them. Their weapons, their hulls, their thinking engines, if such things can be recovered."

"The Order will pay a bounty for each, for the sake of knowing what we face."

Nobody in the half-ring objects. Some of the Knight-Leaders look at their hands.

The curate closes with a blessing. The chamber empties quickly; none stay to confer. Enarms waits by the door until the last of them have gone, then falls into step beside you on the long ramp down.

He does not speak until you are past the guards.
options: kolCh1_walkout2:"That went about as well as expected."

text:
"Better," he says. "They listened. They will watch. That is not nothing." He walks a few more steps. "It is not a ship, either. Or a Knight. Or a single credit."

He sighs. "We keep losing ground with every cycle. The council can vote that away no more than it can vote away the dark. This stalemate cannot hold forever, captain."

"I am not permitted to commission the Order's patrols on my own judgement." He considers the inlay of a wall panel. "But there is no stricture against arranging for patrols to be going the same direction you are. I will think on that."

Enarms stops walking.

"Libra was written off," he says. "You heard it. Not disowned. Written off. The Order cannot afford it, and the Master is right that we cannot." He touches the cord at his wrist. "But I spend my nights studying, captain, and I am sure of this. There is no instruction anywhere against accepting charity on a battlestation's behalf."

He looks at you for a long moment, seemingly torn between a smile and a frown. "I will not order it of you. I will only say that we will gladly accept whatever you can do for Martins and his people." He pauses, as though ashamed of the request to come. "Please do what you can."
"His light upon you, captain. Sister Greenflight is expecting you; I made certain of that much."
"There is a delay at Lyra," Enarms says, reading a message on his slate with a frown. "The Office of Agents will send word. I will send for you again."
Enarms walks you as far as the shuttle bay, and watches you board.

Sister Rebecca Greenflight answers the comm herself. The office behind her is spare: a reliquary on a shelf, a wall of sealed files, a narrow window full of the Eos gate. A slate on her desk illuminates the seal of the Council of Cygnus.

"Captain $playerName." She does not need to look it up. "Brother Enarms' freelancer. Master Helensis' volunteer. Welcome. You have been busy at Cygnus."
options: kolCh1_greenflight2:"The council sent me to report to you."

text:
You give her the same account you gave the council. She listens without interrupting, without taking notes. And you're pretty sure without blinking.

"Machine armadas at a dark star. Scouts at a station we hide from the charts. Raiders carrying our schedules." Her eyes go once to the wall of sealed files behind her. "Enarms sent me that dossier some time ago, with a very careful letter. He has always been quick to see a hand in the dark. Sometimes his vision is keen."

"You will forgive me, captain, if I do not take a freelancer's account and a Knight-Captain's fears as a revelation. The Inquisition has heard of a great many enemies. Most of them were men with debts."
options: kolCh1_greenflight3:"What would you need to convince you?"

text: "Evidence I can hold," she says. "Logs. Wreckage. Names. If what you saw at that star is real, it came from somewhere."

She turns a stylus over in her fingers. "The Order is poorly placed to find where. We are not students of humanity's old sins, and we keep little company with those who are."

"The Academy does, and we will not pretend to approve, but they are not fools. The scholars pick over the rotten carcass of the Domain, but what they find they keep honestly."

A faint dryness. "The Church and the Academy disagree about a great many things, but we will not condemn them simply for the pursuit of knowledge, however misguided. Seek allies there, captain. They will speak more freely to a starfarer than to a Sister of the Order."

"You have been to the place the cynics call Alpha Site." It is not a question; somewhere in the wall of sealed files behind her is a vivid record of it.

"Whatever trial you faced there, you returned intact. We have reason to believe there is more. Be wary, captain. Whatever it is that waits in that darkness, it is not passive. Things that hide at the edge of a system rarely do so by accident."

"Go back. Search the reaches, far out where no one patrols. A starfarer's instruments may catch what a careful eye misses; I am told a neutrino detector might hear a pebble across an ocean." 

"I would send my own agents, but a flight of the Faith's ships to that system would be watched by every eye across the sector. One mercenary is gossip - a dozen Knights is a declaration. My office prefers subtler methods."
[PLACEHOLDER: the player has already begun the Tri-Tachyon trail (the Ninaya is beaten). Greenflight reacts to what they have found so far and points them onward. To be written with Chapter 2.]

Something in her face changes very slightly, the look of someone filing a thing away rather than dismissing it. "Bring me what you find, captain. I will not promise to believe you, but I will promise to investigate it."
"Captain." Enarms glances past the lens at something you can't see. "Not on this channel. A shuttle is waiting at your collar. I will meet you when you're ready."
"Captain." He does not mention the oath. "The shuttle is still yours to call, whenever you have an answer for me."
"Providence smiles on us." Enarms' voice is too warm to be the full truth. "Whatever you saw, don't tell me over the comm. Take the shuttle to my section."
"Captain. Our traders are still being attacked." He holds up a slate you can't read. "If you have time for them, the shuttle knows the way."
"Captain." Enarms is in what passes for a formal Knightly suit, which you have rarely seen. "The room is ready. The shuttle will bring you to the council chambers."

"The Order has begun asking the right questions. I would like to think that is your doing. What can I do for you?"

"Yesterday we held a prayer for your success, captain, and providence has guided you back. It is thanks to your efforts that our insight has blossomed to understanding. Our shields are gleaming and our arms are renewed."

"We would be honored to share this bounty with you. You'll find the Knightly ships you requisition from us will now keep pace with the most modern of the sector."

"Please, continue with your donations; we are so close to a new chapter for the Faith, blessed in God's light."
